note: Rejudged 2026-10-31 by an auditor who authored none of the change. RFC 5303 Section 3.2: "If the system ID and Extended Local Circuit ID of the neighboring system are known (in adjacency three-way state Initializing or Up), the neighbor's system ID SHALL be reported in the Neighbor System ID field, and the neighbor's Extended Local Circuit ID SHALL be reported in the Neighbor Extended Local Circuit ID field." b77067bc31 changed only the call sites in this unit: threeWayTLV and buildP2PHello now take a p2pNeighbor (systemID, extendedCircuitID) instead of a bare SystemID, with the zero value where none was passed before; every assertion is byte-identical and an independent judge approved the change. Verdict unchanged. Earlier judgment follows. Forbidden: omitting the neighbor's System ID from the transmitted IIH when the neighbor is known (Initializing or Up). circuit TestRFC5303SentIIHEchoesKnownNeighbor decodes the sent TLV 240: no Neighbor System ID before any neighbor is heard (negative), and the peer's System ID present in Initializing and again in Up (positive). The adjacency is driven by received Hellos through Circuit.Receive, closing the earlier gap (p2pThreeWayState's haveNeighbor result was unasserted). Recorded + on p2pThreeWayState and - on hello.go threeWayTLV. The row's clause is the System ID only; the Extended Local Circuit ID half of the sentence's condition is not asserted here.
